name: Stablecoin issuance
what_it_is: Issuing the dollar token and holding the reserves behind it.
value_capture: Yield on reserve assets, scaled by float.
why_it_might_not_capture: Reserve yield is a rate bet wearing a payments costume. The economics halve if policy rates fall, regardless of how much the rail is used.
weekly_metric: total stablecoin supply and issuer share

name: Base settlement layer
what_it_is: The chains on which transfers finally settle.
value_capture: Base fees and, indirectly, value accruing to the native asset.
listed_candidates_unscreened: listed proxies are indirect; the assets themselves are not equities
why_it_might_not_capture: CONFIRMED 2026-08-12, and it is the section's central finding. x402 added batched settlement in May 2026: many small claims are verified off-chain and redeemed on-chain in bulk, explicitly because a $0.0001 call cannot clear on-chain at a few cents a transaction. Agent request volume and settlement transaction count are therefore decoupled by design, so per-request micropayments do not imply per-request on-chain settlement. Base fees also remain congestion prices, so abundant throughput and large aggregate fees stay close to mutually exclusive.
weekly_metric: median fee and settled transaction count on payment-oriented chains, read against agent request growth to test whether the two decouple as batching predicts

name: Payment orchestration and APIs
what_it_is: The layer that hides the chain from the merchant: accounts, conversion, payouts, compliance plumbing.
value_capture: Take rate on volume, which is the classic payments economic.
why_it_might_not_capture: Take rates compress once the rail is commoditised, and the incumbents building it already have the merchants.

name: Edge and traffic distribution
what_it_is: Whoever sits in front of the request and decides which rail it uses. The finding from the Cloudflare call is that this is a distribution question, not a technology one.
value_capture: Per-request toll on machine traffic, plus the right to set the standard — and as at 2026-08-12 Cloudflare co-governs the x402 Foundation with Coinbase, so it is setting the standard rather than merely sitting in front of it. Monetization Gateway is waitlist-only with no disclosed pricing, so nothing is yet earned.
listed_candidates_unscreened: Cloudflare, and the browser and agent-framework owners
why_it_might_not_capture: A per-request toll may never need per-request settlement, and batching now confirms it does not. That strengthens this layer at the settlement layer's expense: the edge keeps the metering relationship and the chain below sees far fewer transactions than the traffic figures imply. The unresolved risk is different — the toll is only worth what agents will pay, and the monetizable share is management's own 1-10% estimate on traffic whose agent-versus-crawler split Cloudflare has not published.
weekly_metric: non-human share of web traffic and per-request payment protocol adoption

name: Merchant acceptance and acquiring
what_it_is: Getting real sellers to accept the token and getting them paid in what they want.
listed_candidates_unscreened: listed acquirers and payment service providers
why_it_might_not_capture: The hardest and least glamorous part of every payments story, and the one that has defeated most previous attempts.
weekly_metric: named merchant acceptance announcements with volume disclosed

name: Card network defensive layer
what_it_is: The existing networks adding stablecoin settlement legs rather than being displaced by them.
value_capture: Preservation of existing take rate, with a new settlement back end.
why_it_might_not_capture: Partly answered 2026-08-12, and against the displacement thesis: Visa and Mastercard are both members of the x402 Foundation. The incumbents are inside the standard rather than being routed around by it, which is what the defensive case predicted. This remains the layer that can neutralise the thesis by cutting its fixed-fee floor for machine-initiated payments.
weekly_metric: card network stablecoin settlement disclosures in filings

name: Custody, attestation and compliance
what_it_is: Holding keys, proving reserves, and satisfying travel-rule and KYC obligations.
value_capture: Fee on assets held and per-transaction compliance charges.
why_it_might_not_capture: Regulated, capital-intensive and priced like infrastructure rather than software.
weekly_metric: reserve attestation cadence and custody disclosures

name: Agent identity and delegated authority
what_it_is: Proving which agent is acting for which principal, with what spending limit and what recourse. Largely unbuilt.
value_capture: Undetermined. Could be a standard nobody owns, or the most defensible position in the stack.
why_it_might_not_capture: May resolve into an open standard with no owner, which is the most likely outcome for identity layers historically.
weekly_metric: named standards activity and protocol adoption
